provenance: Real ESA Anomaly Dataset (ESA-ADB) telemetry, Mission1 lightweight channels 41-46. Kotowski et al., 'European Space Agency Dataset and Benchmark for Real-World Anomaly Detection in Spacecraft Time Series', Journal of Data-centric Machine Learning Research (DMLR), 2026 (earlier version: arXiv:2406.17826). Data: De Canio, Kotowski & Haskamp, 'ESA Anomaly Dataset', Zenodo record 12528696 (2024), CC BY 3.0 IGO. One contiguous stretch of the test half (ESA-ADB's own Mission1 split from 2007-01-01, in the corpus's anonymised calendar): 8,640 rows at 30s after 8 rows of history. Chosen, among the stretches stepping by three hours that hold an anomaly past their first 2,100 rows, as the one where the student's pipeline detects the most anomalies (then the most events, the fewest false alarms, the earliest), so that the page has flags to reproduce: its score here is a reproduction check, and the student's measurement is its record's, over the whole test half. z-scored with the constants the student publishes, rounded to 4 decimals; neither model trained on any of it.
split: one contiguous stretch of the held-out test half, ESA-ADB's own Mission1 split from 2007-01-01: the three days where the student's pipeline detects the most anomalies, so that the page has flags to reproduce
attribution: Kotowski et al., 'European Space Agency Dataset and Benchmark for Real-World Anomaly Detection in Spacecraft Time Series', Journal of Data-centric Machine Learning Research (DMLR), 2026 (earlier version: arXiv:2406.17826). Data: De Canio, Kotowski & Haskamp, 'ESA Anomaly Dataset', Zenodo record 12528696 (2024), CC BY 3.0 IGO.
modifications: Channels 41 to 46 of ESA-ADB Mission1, resampled to 30 s by zero-order hold and z-scored with the mean and standard deviation of the unlabelled training rows; one contiguous stretch of 8,640 rows of the held-out test half (from 2007-01-01, ESA-ADB's own split) after 8 rows of history, rounded to 4 decimals, with the annotations of these channels that start and end inside it, their times in milliseconds.

expected.note: Computed from these rows as shipped, with the forecast summed term by term in the page's order, so the page reproduces the flags exactly; the event scores are ESA-ADB's corrected event-wise F0.5 over this stretch alone, so they are not the test half's. The forecast is the student's: the page evaluates the same dot products under CKKS and reports how far the decrypted forecast moves.
